content.title: About
content.content: Meatless Lo Mein is a ready‑to‑cook package of wheat‑based noodles, vegetables and aromatic spices, designed for vegetarians and vegans. It is served as stir‑fried noodles with a savory sauce that mimics the classic Chinese dish, but without any meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lo Mein is a staple of Chinese cuisine, and the vegetarian version appeared in the 1970s in response to growing demand for plant‑based alternatives.
The noodles are produced by extrusion, giving them a firm bite and reducing the tendency to stick together.
The dried vegetable mix often includes carrot, cabbage, onion and mushrooms, providing bright colour and crunch after cooking.
Thanks to soy sauce and umami‑rich ingredients, meatless Lo Mein retains the deep flavour typical of the traditional dish.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Wheat noodles contain little saturated fat, making the dish more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Vegetable additions (carrot, cabbage) boost fiber content, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Plant‑based protein
items.content: Soy sauce and optional tofu provide a modest amount of complete protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat noodles and vegetables supply B1, B2 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low sugar
items.content: The product contains no added sugars, suitable for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Soy sauce allergy
items.content: Soy sauce can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with soy allergy.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate content
items.content: Some sauce variants contain added MSG, which may cause sensitivity in certain people.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Wheat noodles have a high glycemic index, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Soy sauce adds significant sodium; low‑sodium versions are recommended for salt‑restricted diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat a small amount of vegetable oil in a pan, add the noodles and stir‑fry for 2‑3 minutes. Then add the vegetable mix and sauce, continue cooking until the vegetables are tender, about 5‑7 minutes. Optional additions include tofu, bean sprouts or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry package in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. Once opened, use within 3‑4 months. Cooked Lo Mein should be refrigerated and consumed within 2 days.
